comparison: Perfect agreement on cryo-EM claims (C49-C52). OpenEval rated as UNCERTAIN due to low resolution and contradictory data, while peer reviewers explicitly praised the authors for conducting follow-up experiments that failed to confirm initial speculative models, viewing this as strengthening the work.

Perfect agreement on RGD motif reinterpretation (C93-C96). Both OpenEval and peer reviewers found the structural evidence convincing that RGD motifs are buried and not surface-exposed, supporting reinterpretation of previous findings.

Perfect agreement on rigid stalk model and distance hypothesis (C34, C87, C97-C101). OpenEval rated as UNCERTAIN noting lack of direct experimental validation, while peer reviewers found the model well-supported by in vivo data and impactful for the field.

Strong agreement on major structural findings (C32, C35, C36, C42, C73). Both found the crystallographic structure well-supported. Peer review also included C43-C44 from the same structural analysis, describing it as 'beautiful' and 'valuable structural data.'

Strong agreement on functional decoupling discovery (C33, C89-C92, C102). Both found this major conceptual advance well-supported. Peer reviewers described it as 'exciting and well supported' with consistency in findings, while OpenEval noted two independent lines of evidence.

Moderate agreement on domain deletion analysis (C55-C57, C59-C63). Both found the systematic deletion experiments convincing with appropriate replication and statistical analysis. Peer review emphasized integration of data and rigor of in vivo experiments.

Partial agreement on binding cleft mutation experiments (C70-C71). Both found these experiments well-executed. OpenEval focused on these as part of functional decoupling evidence, while peer reviewers noted they help interpret the mechanism of the conserved site.

Agreement on COI domain protective mechanism (C82-C83). Both found the AlphaFold prediction supportive of experimental observations. OpenEval noted the mechanism is somewhat speculative but structurally supported, while peer reviewers found the integration of structural and functional data convincing.
Agreement on absence of BAR domain and substrate binding (C76-C77). Both accepted these structural comparisons as well-supported observations from the crystal structure without raising concerns.

Agreement on detailed structural features (C45-C47). Both found these crystallographic details well-supported. OpenEval noted good refinement statistics, while peer reviewers described the structure as 'beautiful' with 'good level of rigor.'
Agreement on domain deletion summary (C84-C86). Both found the complete loss of function with all Ig-domains deleted and strong decreases with single deletions well-supported by the data in Figure 3.

Agreement on protein stability findings (C64-C67). Both found the western blot data convincing for explaining functional defects. OpenEval emphasized decoupling of aggregation from biofilm/conjugation, while peer reviewers noted consistency with overall study rigor.
Agreement on COI domain instability (C80-C81). Both found the western blot data clearly showing PrgBΔCOI instability convincing and consistent with the comprehensive phenotypic characterization.
Agreement on eDNA binding control (C72). Both found this EMSA control experiment rigorous and supportive of the interpretation that the conserved site has functions beyond DNA binding.

Partial overlap on binding cleft mutations (C68-C69). OpenEval grouped these with C70-C72 as evidence for functional decoupling, while peer reviewers included them with broader functional decoupling claims (C88-C92), finding them exciting and well-supported.

Partial overlap on structural features (C43-C44). OpenEval included these with broader structural details (C38-C48), while peer reviewers grouped them with major structural findings, all described as valuable and convincing.

Partial overlap on complementation controls (C53-C54). OpenEval included these in broader deletion analysis (C53-C67), while peer reviewers specifically noted these controls as part of well-designed experimental approach.

Minimal overlap on metal binding (C48). OpenEval included this with detailed structural features, while peer reviewers grouped it with structural comparisons and distinctions from homologous proteins.

OpenEval evaluated background and literature claims (C1-C23) as SUPPORTED, providing context for the study. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as peer reviewers focused on novel findings rather than background claims.

OpenEval evaluated authors' previous work citations (C24-C31) as SUPPORTED background. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as peer reviewers did not separately assess these foundational claims.
OpenEval evaluated PrgB dimerization observation (C37) as SUPPORTED based on chromatography data. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this specific biochemical characterization.
